English: Steam Pit
A primitive earth-dug pit lined with stones and canvas, heated by nearby fires. The early nomadic approach to communal cleansing and warmth, fostering basic unity and comfort at camp.
Hot Stone Hut
A simple felt hut with heated stones at its heart, used by clansfolk to sweat out impurities and strengthen bonds. Offers improved health and unity over a basic steam pit.
Heated Pavilion
A large, mobile tent with improved stone braziers and partitions, serving as a communal bathing and meeting place, greatly boosting morale and hygiene across the camp.
Bath Chamber
A semi-permanent wooden bathhouse with dedicated steam chambers and changing areas. A mark of rising sophistication among the nomads, it draws families together and increases the tribes resilience.
Changing Room
A refined facility with stone floors, private changing stalls, and improved steam distribution. The clans elite gather here, fostering unity and pride.
Warm Hall
A large, permanent heated hall crafted from timber and brick, offering communal baths, massage rooms, and dedicated hearths—greatly enhancing population growth, unity, and supply capacity.
Scented Room
A luxury chamber infused with aromatic herbs, decorated walls, and heated marble. The air itself encourages fertility and unity, making this a jewel of nomadic culture.
Family Bathhouse
A grand structure with separate wings for families, ornate pools, and social spaces. Deepens clan bonds, enhances supply, and encourages rapid population growth.
Community Bath Hall
A vast domed bath complex, richly adorned with mosaics and equipped for hundreds. The center of nomadic life and diplomacy, offering unmatched unity and growth.
Iranian Grand Hammam

The pinnacle of bathhouse tradition: a monumental marble hammam featuring domed steam rooms, fountains, and gardens. Greatly impresses all clans, substantially boosts population, and is famed as a symbol of Persian-inspired nomadic splendor.
